findings.explanation: The NSX native load balancer on Edge nodes runs NGINX (config at /config/vmware/edge/lb/etc/<instance>/nginx.conf, logs under /var/log/lb/). It is not HAProxy, and /var/log/edge_lb.log is not a documented path. The same HAProxy claim runs through the title-driven text, dataSources, equipment and hardware.
findings.quote: Provision syslog receivers tailing **`/var/log/edge_lb.log`** from each Edge VM or bare-metal transport node carrying HAProxy narratives
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the dataplane as NGINX-based. Source LB logs from Edge syslog (load-balancer access/error logs forwarded via the Edge syslog exporter) or /var/log/lb/, and remove 'HAProxy' from dataSources, equipment ('haproxy') and hardware. Note that the native LB is deprecated in favour of VMware Avi Load Balancer.

findings.explanation: In the Policy API, pool status is GET /policy/api/v1/infra/lb-services/{lb-service-id}/lb-pools/{lb-pool-id}/detailed-status, returning AggregateLBPoolStatus. Pool member status values are UP, DOWN, DISABLED, GRACEFUL_DISABLED, UNUSED and UNKNOWN; DRAINING does not exist. The virtual-server path is likewise lb-services/{id}/lb-virtual-servers/{id}/detailed-status.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the lb-services/{id}/lb-pools/{id}/detailed-status and lb-virtual-servers/{id}/detailed-status paths. Replace DRAINING with GRACEFUL_DISABLED, and note that min_active_members is a pool configuration field (GET /infra/lb-pools/{id}), not a status field.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4241 is the 'VMware NSX-T Splunk App' built by VMware NSX Logging. It is a dashboard app for NSX syslog, not a 'Splunk Add-on' (Splunk_TA_vmware-nsxt), and it does not poll LB status REST endpoints or create vmware:nsxt:lb_pool_status. The grounding guide's ID 4856 is also wrong (it is the Metrics Add-on for Infrastructure), so the guide needs correcting too.
findings.quote: **Splunk Add-on for VMware NSX-T** ([Splunkbase 4241](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4241)) for **`vmware:nsxt:*`** parsing
findings.suggested_fix: Name 4241 correctly as the VMware NSX-T Splunk App (syslog dashboards). State that the lb_pool_status and lb_vs_status sourcetypes come from a custom REST collector (rest_ta or a scripted input) that the adopter must build.

findings.explanation: This sentence is repeated sixteen times, after a section literally titled 'Padding narrative'. It is followed by a 'Bold glossary reinforcement' list of template phrases ('Annotate X watchers beside Y overlays referencing Z governance cues'), and the final Step 1 / Step 2 block repeats the app and dataSources text verbatim. About half the field is filler.
findings.quote: Extend readiness dossiers referencing rehearsed failover swaps annotated inside tabletop CRQ identifiers distinct from cold migrations logged inside virtualization consoles.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the padding, governance supplements, glossary and duplicated Step 1 / Step 2 boilerplate. Keep the prerequisites, ingestion, search design, validation and runbook sections, corrected for the facts above.

findings.explanation: Pool and virtual-server status snapshots are availability state, not network flows (Network_Traffic) or host CPU, memory or storage metrics (Performance). The schema text maps the VIP to 'destination_ip', which is not a CIM field (CIM uses dest_ip).
findings.suggested_fix: Leave cimModels empty, or state that no CIM model applies. Drop the schema and dataModelAcceleration text that maps monitor_interval_sec to 'duration'.

findings.explanation: The SPL never reads ACI or Palo Alto data. These sources, and the matching equipment and equipmentModels entries (cisco_aci, cisco_nexus, paloalto_pan_firewall), add noise and wrongly widen the UC's scope.
findings.quote: optional **`sourcetype=cisco:aci:syslog`** cross-tags when east-west VIPs front ACI **`fvAEPg`** workloads—correlation only; **`sourcetype=paloalto:firewall`** (optional)
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the ACI and Palo Alto sourcetypes from dataSources and the related equipment and equipmentModels entries.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by an automated reviewer ('agent-handcraft-2026-04-29'), yet the API paths, member enums and dataplane are wrong and the SPL does not parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft until an NSX SME validates the collector and search.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `| eval story=pool_fault." | ".edge_id." | ".pool_id"` ends with an unbalanced double quote, leaving an unterminated string literal. The search fails to parse.

pool_fault tests member_txt IN ("DOWN","DRAINING","DISABLED"), but NSX reports GRACEFUL_DISABLED and UNUSED, never DRAINING. The lb_log_sev branches regex-match HAProxy-style tokens in a log the NSX NGINX dataplane does not produce.

Two logic problems. monitor_interval_jitter flags any configured interval other than 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60 seconds, which is a non-standard setting rather than jitter. dc(pool_fault) is computed while grouping BY pool_fault, so fault_cardinality is always 1.

summary: The UC is built on wrong product facts. The NSX native load balancer is NGINX-based, not HAProxy, and the Policy API status paths, member-state enums and Splunkbase add-on identity are all incorrect. detailedImplementation is padded with a sentence repeated sixteen times and a generated 'glossary', and the SPL has an unterminated string literal.
